column1: An explorer’s encounter with the ruined city of Machu Picchu, the most famous icon of the Inca civilisation
column2: 一位探险家与马丘比丘古城遗址的相遇。这座遗址是印加文明最著名的象征。

column1: When the US explorer and academic Hiram Bingham arrived in South America in 1911, he was ready for what was to be the greatest achievement of his life: the exploration of the remote hinterland to the west of Cusco, the old capital of the Inca empire in the Andes mountains of Peru.
column2: 1911年，美国探险家兼学者海勒姆·宾厄姆来到南美洲，准备展开日后成为他毕生最大成就的探索：考察秘鲁安第斯山脉中、印加帝国故都库斯科以西的偏远腹地。
column3: explorer and academic|探险家兼学者

column1: His goal was to locate the remains of a city called Vitcos, the last capital of the Inca civilisation.
column2: 他的目标是找到维特科斯城的遗迹，那是印加文明最后的都城。

column1: Cusco lies on a high plateau at an elevation of more than 3,000 metres, and Bingham’s plan was to descend from this plateau along the valley of the Urubamba river, which takes a circuitous route down to the Amazon and passes through an area of dramatic canyons and mountain ranges.
column2: 库斯科位于海拔超过3000米的高原上。宾厄姆打算沿乌鲁班巴河谷从高原向低处走。这条河一路蜿蜒流向亚马孙河，途中穿过峡谷险峻、群山耸立的地区。

column1: When Bingham and his team set off down the Urubamba in late July, they had an advantage over travellers who had preceded them: a track had recently been blasted down the valley canyon to enable rubber to be brought up by mules from the jungle.
column2: 7月底，宾厄姆和他的队伍沿乌鲁班巴河出发。他们比此前到过这里的旅行者占了一个便宜：不久前，人们已在峡谷中炸开一条小道，以便用骡子将橡胶从丛林里驮运上来。
column4: had an advantage over|比……占优势

column1: Almost all previous travellers had left the river at Ollantaytambo and taken a high pass across the mountains to rejoin the river lower down, thereby cutting a substantial corner, but also therefore never passing through the area around Machu Picchu.
column2: 此前几乎所有旅行者都在奥扬泰坦博离开河道，翻过高处的山口，随后在下游再次沿河前进。这样固然抄了很大一段近道，却也因此从未经过马丘比丘一带。
column5: rejoin the river|回到河边继续走
column7: cutting a substantial corner|抄了一大段近道

column1: On 24 July they were a few days into their descent of the valley.
column2: 到7月24日，他们沿山谷向下已经走了几天。
column3: a few days into|已进行了几天

column1: The day began slowly, with Bingham trying to arrange sufficient mules for the next stage of the trek.
column2: 这一天开始得很慢，宾厄姆正设法为下一段艰苦行程安排足够的骡子。

column1: His companions showed no interest in accompanying him up the nearby hill to see some ruins that a local farmer, Melchor Arteaga, had told them about the night before.
column2: 当地农民梅尔乔尔·阿尔特亚加前一晚曾提到附近山上有些废墟，但宾厄姆的同伴毫无兴趣陪他上山去看。
column4: showed no interest in|对……没有兴趣

column1: The morning was dull and damp, and Bingham also seems to have been less than keen on the prospect of climbing the hill.
column2: 那天早晨阴沉潮湿，宾厄姆自己似乎也不大热衷于爬这座山。
column5: less than keen on|对……并不热衷

column1: In his book Lost City of the Incas, he relates that he made the ascent without having the least expectation that he would find anything at the top.
column2: 在《印加失落之城》一书中，他回忆说，自己上山时根本没有指望在山顶发现什么。
column5: the least expectation|哪怕一点期待

column1: Bingham writes about the approach in vivid style in his book.
column2: 书中，宾厄姆把走近遗址的过程描写得十分生动。

column1: First, as he climbs up the hill, he describes the ever-present possibility of deadly snakes, ‘capable of making considerable springs when in pursuit of their prey’; not that he sees any.
column2: 他先写上山时随时可能遇到致命的毒蛇，这些蛇“追捕猎物时能蹿出很远”；不过，他其实并没有看见蛇。

column1: Then there’s a sense of mounting discovery as he comes across great sweeps of terraces, then a mausoleum, followed by monumental staircases and, finally, the grand ceremonial buildings of Machu Picchu.
column2: 接下来，随着他发现连绵成片的梯田，一种不断有新发现的感觉油然而生。随后他看到一座陵墓、宏伟的阶梯，最后是马丘比丘庄严的礼仪建筑群。
column5: great sweeps of terraces|连绵成片的梯田

column1: ‘It seemed like an unbelievable dream ... the sight held me spellbound ...’ he wrote.
column2: “这简直像一个难以置信的梦……眼前的景象令我出神……”他写道。
column5: held me spellbound|让我看得入迷

column1: We should remember, however, that Lost City of the Incas is a work of hindsight, not written until 1948, many years after his journey.
column2: 不过，我们应当记得，《印加失落之城》是事后回顾之作，直到1948年才写成，距那次旅程已有多年。
column3: a work of hindsight|事后回顾之作

column1: His journal entries of the time reveal a much more gradual appreciation of his achievement.
column2: 他当时的日记显示，他对自己这次成就的认识其实是逐渐形成的。

column1: He spent the afternoon at the ruins noting down the dimensions of some of the buildings, then descended and rejoined his companions, to whom he seems to have said little about his discovery.
column2: 他把那天下午花在遗址上，记下几座建筑的尺寸，然后下山与同伴会合。对于自己的发现，他似乎并没有对他们说多少。

column1: At this stage, Bingham didn’t realise the extent or the importance of the site, nor did he realise what use he could make of the discovery.
column2: 在这个阶段，宾厄姆既没意识到遗址规模有多大、意义有多重要，也没想到自己能如何利用这项发现。
column7: what use he could make of|他能怎样利用

column1: However, soon after returning it occurred to him that he could make a name for himself from this discovery.
column2: 不过，回去后不久，他就想到，自己可以借这项发现成名。
column4: it occurred to him|他突然想到
column5: make a name for himself|为自己赢得声名

column1: When he came to write the National Geographic magazine article that broke the story to the world in April 1913, he knew he had to produce a big idea.
column2: 1913年4月，《国家地理》杂志刊发了他向全世界披露这项发现的文章。动笔写作时，他知道自己得提出一个足够引人注目的说法。
column5: broke the story|首次披露这一消息
column6: produce a big idea|提出引人注目的构想

column1: He wondered whether it could have been the birthplace of the very first Inca, Manco the Great, and whether it could also have been what chroniclers described as ‘the last city of the Incas’.
column2: 他猜想，这里会不会是印加第一位君主曼科大帝的出生地，也会不会就是编年史家所说的“印加人最后的城市”。
column5: the very first Inca|印加第一位君主

column1: This term refers to Vilcabamba, the settlement where the Incas had fled from Spanish invaders in the 1530s.
column2: 这个称呼指的是比尔卡班巴，即16世纪30年代印加人为躲避西班牙入侵者而逃往的聚居地。
column7: in the 1530s|在十六世纪三十年代

column1: Bingham made desperate attempts to prove this belief for nearly 40 years.
column2: 近40年里，宾厄姆都在竭尽全力设法证明自己的看法。

column1: Sadly, his vision of the site as both the beginning and end of the Inca civilisation, while a magnificent one, is inaccurate.
column2: 遗憾的是，他把这处遗址视为印加文明的起点和终点，这一设想虽宏大，却并不准确。
column4: both the beginning and end|起点和终点两者

column1: We now know that Vilcabamba actually lies 65 kilometres away in the depths of the jungle.
column2: 如今我们知道，比尔卡班巴实际在65公里之外，位于丛林深处。

column1: One question that has perplexed visitors, historians and archaeologists alike ever since Bingham, is why the site seems to have been abandoned before the Spanish Conquest.
column2: 自宾厄姆以来，一个问题一直令游客、历史学家和考古学家同样困惑：为什么这处遗址似乎在西班牙人征服当地之前就已遭弃用？

column1: There are no references to it by any of the Spanish chroniclers — and if they had known of its existence so close to Cusco they would certainly have come in search of gold.
column2: 西班牙编年史家的记载都没提到它。要是他们知道离库斯科这么近的地方有这样一座城，肯定早就来寻找黄金了。

column1: An idea which has gained wide acceptance over the past few years is that Machu Picchu was a moya, a country estate built by an Inca emperor to escape the cold winters of Cusco, where the elite could enjoy monumental architecture and spectacular views.
column2: 过去几年间，一种看法得到广泛认同：马丘比丘是一处“莫亚”，即一位印加皇帝为躲避库斯科寒冬而建的乡间庄园，上层人士可以在那里欣赏宏伟的建筑和壮丽的景色。
column3: gained wide acceptance|得到广泛认可
column4: moya|n. 印加君主的乡间庄园

column1: Furthermore, the particular architecture of Machu Picchu suggests that it was constructed at the time of the greatest of all the Incas, the emperor Pachacuti (c. 1438-71).
column2: 此外，马丘比丘独特的建筑风格显示，它很可能建于最伟大的印加君主帕查库蒂在位时（约1438—1471年）。

column1: By custom, Pachacuti’s descendants built other similar estates for their own use, and so Machu Picchu would have been abandoned after his death, some 50 years before the Spanish Conquest.
column2: 按照习俗，帕查库蒂的后代为自己另建同类庄园。因此，马丘比丘当是在他去世后遭到弃用的，那是在西班牙人征服当地之前约50年。
column6: for their own use|供他们自己使用
column7: would have been abandoned|推想当时已被弃用
